task.name: mysql live
task.start: Pointed at this file, in any session the operator chooses (rules kickoff), you build from the files alone: on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin, read them whole before you write anything, and take nothing said earlier in the session, or remembered from other work, as authority. Your label is <model>-<effort> as the root's method model says. Read whole, in this order (root method read): every .rs file and every Cargo.toml under crates/, engines/ and tools/ as merged on main; specs/root.xml; specs/rules.xml; this file; then the files it names. Cut the branch SF-121-mysql-live-v1-<model>-<effort> from the head of main. Every commit message starts with SF-121 and carries no attribution of any kind; commit, push and open the PR under the GitHub account of whoever runs the build (decision service-accounts). Build what this file says, run its gates, push the branch and open the PR into main titled "SF-121 mysql live v1 · <model>-<effort>" with the body the root's method pr lists. Show on the screen, as it happens, each step by its number and name, each test run with its result, and each gate. What this file, the root, the rules and the merged code do not say is a stop, not a guess.
task.piece: A schema read live by the scope the person chose, the server's version first and only what that version has, gently, with metadata and, when the server keeps it, usage; every step reported as it happens. In the engine interface: the scope, the catalog sources an engine declares for each version, and the scoped live read with its source, its metadata and usage, and its steps; the kit requiring the catalog sources. In MySQL: 5.7 as its oldest version, with what 5.7 lacks found in a schema for it; its catalog sources; its scoped read on 5.7, 8.0, 8.4, 9.7 and the later releases, never inside the database it reads; performance_schema's usage as the server gives it; and a connection test naming the grants this version needs. Nothing else: no store, no table written, no screen (the read screen is the canvas's, t10).
task.before: Merged on main: MySQL's tables (t04) and everything before them; the design that keeps what this read returns: schema/cortex/source_reads.sql, the owner features/usage, and the decisions live-first, mysql-versions, version-facts, usage-apart, gentle-read, read-scope and read-screen.
task.after: The store (t07) writes a read's source to cortex.source_reads, its definitions as one import turn, and its metadata and usage as a snapshot of the owner usage; the canvas (t10) shows its steps as the read screen.

module.public: Scope, CatalogSource, Source, ReadStep, ObjectUsage, IndexUsage, Digest, Usage, LiveRead; Live::catalog_sources and Live::read_live
module.step: Scope { metadata: bool, usage: bool, kinds: Option<Vec<String>>, objects: Option<Vec<String>> }: definitions are always read; metadata adds sizes and statistics; usage adds what the server measured; kinds names the kinds of object to read, as the engine's kinds name them, None for all; objects names the objects to read, each a name or a pattern in which % is any run of characters and _ one character, compared as the server names them, None for all. Scope::everything() is every part, every kind and object; Scope::definitions() is definitions alone. to_json() gives {"everything": true} for everything() and otherwise {"parts": [...], "kinds": [...], "objects": [...]}, parts always holding "definitions" and holding "metadata" and "usage" when set, kinds and objects left out when None; from_json() reads both back, and refuses anything else with the error `not a read scope: <what is wrong>`. Scope::takes(kind, name) is true when the kind and the name are both read.

step.name: what an engine asks, as data

module.step: CatalogSource { source: &'static str, gives: &'static str, needs: Option<&'static str>, usage: bool }, the shape of a row of cortex.catalog_sources: the catalog table or statement as the server names it, what the read takes from it, the grant it needs beyond the database's own (None for none), and whether it is a source of metadata or usage. Live::catalog_sources(&self, version: &str) -> Vec<CatalogSource>, in the order the read asks them.

Live::read_live(&self, profile: &Profile, secret: Option<&Secret>, database: &str, scope: &Scope, limit: Duration, progress: &mut dyn FnMut(&ReadStep)) -> Result<LiveRead, String>. LiveRead { imported: Imported, source: Source, usage: Option<Usage> }: imported holds the definitions the scope takes, read as read() reads them; usage is None unless the scope asks for metadata or usage. Source { server_version, server_edition: Option, read_as, uptime: Option<u64>, usage_available: bool, missing_grants: Vec<String> }, the fields of a cortex.source_reads row by the same names. Usage { source, uptime: u64, digests_lost: u64, settings: Value, objects: Vec<ObjectUsage>, indexes: Vec<IndexUsage>, digests: Vec<Digest> } and ObjectUsage, IndexUsage and Digest hold the columns of usage.snapshots, usage.object_usage, usage.index_usage and usage.query_digests but their ids, snapshot, object, index and taken_at (the store's), by the same names: a count or a time an Option<u64>, picoseconds as the server counts them; a time the server gives an Option<String>, as it gives it; source_row and source_rows a serde_json Value, the server's rows as it gave them. ReadStep { name, why, statements: Vec<String>, found: Vec<(String, String)>, skipped: Option<String> }: a step of the read in words people understand, the statements it sent, what it found as pairs of a value and what it is, and, for a step the scope or the server leaves out, why; progress is called once for each step, in order, as it ends. A read that has taken longer than limit stops after the step it is in, keeps what it read, and reports every step not taken as skipped with `stopped: the read took longer than <limit>`.

An engine with a live part that declares no catalog source for a version it supports is the kit's finding `version <version> declares no catalog source`; a source declared twice for one version is `version <version>: <source> is declared twice`; a source whose gives is empty is `version <version>: <source> gives nothing`.

5.7 is the first of VERSIONS (MySQL 5.7), so every feature available until a later version is available in it. The features 5.7 lacks are declared since 8.0, each with what the person is told: CHECK_CONSTRAINTS ("a CHECK constraint: 5.7 parses it and ignores it"), INVISIBLE ("an invisible column, key or index"), EXPRESSION_PARTS ("an index or key part that is an expression"), DESCENDING_PARTS ("a descending index or key part: 5.7 parses it and ignores it") and SPATIAL_REFERENCE_SYSTEMS ("a spatial reference system of its own"). The spatial reference system kind (engines/mysql/src/kinds.rs) is available as SPATIAL_REFERENCE_SYSTEMS is. engines/mysql/src/checks.rs gives, for a schema whose version lacks one of the first four, the problem `<what> is not in MySQL <version>` on every part that uses it: a check constraint; a column, key or index whose option invisible is true; an index part that is an expression; a key or index part whose desc is true.

catalog_sources(version) is, in order: the version (SELECT VERSION(), @@version_comment, CURRENT_USER(), @@performance_schema); the catalog tables of information_schema the read asks (SCHEMATA, TABLES, COLUMNS, STATISTICS, KEY_COLUMN_USAGE, REFERENTIAL_CONSTRAINTS, VIEWS, ROUTINES, TRIGGERS, EVENTS; CHECK_CONSTRAINTS from 8.0; INNODB_TABLESPACES from 8.0 and INNODB_SYS_TABLESPACES on 5.7; ST_SPATIAL_REFERENCE_SYSTEMS from 8.0; LIBRARIES as the feature LIBRARIES is); SHOW CREATE TABLE, VIEW, PROCEDURE, FUNCTION, TRIGGER and EVENT; then, usage true, information_schema.TABLES and STATISTICS for sizes and statistics, and performance_schema's global_status (the uptime), global_variables, setup_consumers, table_io_waits_summary_by_table, table_lock_waits_summary_by_table, table_io_waits_summary_by_index_usage and events_statements_summary_by_digest. The grants are those of docs/live-mysql.xml's account: SHOW VIEW for views, TRIGGER for triggers, EVENT for events, PROCESS for tablespaces, SELECT ON performance_schema.* for usage; routines need SELECT ON mysql.proc on 5.7 and SHOW_ROUTINE from 8.0.

read_live connects as test does and asks the version first; MariaDB is refused as read() refuses it; the version decides every statement after it, through catalog_sources. The session is opened read only and made to give way before anything else is asked: SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY, SET SESSION lock_wait_timeout = 5 and SET SESSION max_execution_time = 10000, each sent as its own statement. One connection, one statement at a time; no USE, ever: every statement names the database, and the read is never inside the database it reads, so none of its statements is counted with that database's. A view's definition, which the server gives with every name qualified by its database when read from outside it, has `<database>`. removed wherever it qualifies a name outside a string, so it is the definition a dump gives. Nothing that writes, counts the rows of a table, analyses, flushes, truncates or sets anything but the session's own three settings is ever sent.

The definitions read are those the scope takes (Scope::takes on each object's kind and name, as the catalog lists them), each read with SHOW CREATE as read() reads it; an object the scope leaves out is never asked for. With metadata, information_schema.TABLES gives each table's estimated rows, data and index size and last write (UPDATE_TIME), and STATISTICS each index's cardinality (the greatest of its parts'), as the server has them (information_schema_stats_expiry is never changed), into ObjectUsage and IndexUsage with source_rows holding the rows by the table they came from, and Usage.source `information_schema`. With usage, when @@performance_schema is 1 and the account can read it: the uptime, the settings (performance_schema_digests_size, performance_schema_max_digest_length, information_schema_stats_expiry where the version has it, and setup_consumers by name), the rows of the three summary tables whose OBJECT_SCHEMA is the database, and the digests whose SCHEMA_NAME is the database, each kept whole in source_row or source_rows as the server gives it (read as JSON_OBJECT of every column the version's table has), their counts in the typed fields by the usage tables' names, QUANTILE_95, QUANTILE_99, QUANTILE_999, SUM_CPU_TIME and QUERY_SAMPLE_TEXT where the version has them; digests_lost the COUNT_STAR of the row whose DIGEST is NULL; Usage.source `performance_schema`. Without it, usage_available is false and the usage steps are reported skipped with `performance_schema is off` or `the account cannot read performance_schema`.

The steps reported are, in order: the version; what it offers (the catalog tables this version has); the structure; sizes and estimates; table usage; index usage; query digests. A step the scope does not need is reported skipped with `not asked for`. Each ReadStep's statements are those it sent, in order, the session's three settings in the first step's.

The test's Rights step names, for the server's version, every grant of catalog_sources the account lacks for the databases it reads: a grant that leaves definitions unread (SHOW VIEW, TRIGGER, EVENT, and routines' grant for the version) fails it as it does today; one that leaves only metadata or usage unread (PROCESS, SELECT ON performance_schema.*) is a Warning naming the grant and what will not be read. read_live puts the grants missing in Source.missing_grants.

tests.how: Rust tests: those of steps 1 to 6 on values of their own and the engines' declarations, reaching no database (in crates/engine/tests/interface.rs and engines/mysql/tests/live_read.rs, each where its step's code is); those named in Docker start MySQL servers in Docker (mysql:5.7, run as linux/amd64 on a machine that is not, mysql:8.0, mysql:8.4, mysql:9.7), load engines/mysql/tests/samples/live/shop.sql into each, run workload.sql against it, and read it through a profile of the test's own, each server removed when its test ends; they are marked ignored with the reason `needs Docker and the MySQL images`, as engines/mysql/tests/live.rs marks its own.

an engine with a live part and no catalog source for a version it supports is the kit's finding naming the version
5.7 is the oldest version and every feature is in the versions the release notes say
a schema for 5.7 with a check constraint, an invisible column, an expression part or a descending part is a problem for each, saying it is not in MySQL 5.7
every MySQL version declares its catalog sources, 5.7's naming SELECT ON mysql.proc for routines and none of the tables only 8.0 has
in Docker, the shop sample read live from 5.7, 8.0, 8.4 and 9.7 is the same schema as a dump of it read from the same server
in Docker, no statement of the read is counted with the database it reads
in Docker, the read's first statements open a read-only session with a lock wait timeout and a time limit on every statement
in Docker, definitions only sends no statement to performance_schema
in Docker, a scope of one kind reads only that kind, and a scope of named objects only those objects
in Docker, the usage of the shop workload names an index never read and a statement that used no index
in Docker, 5.7's digests carry no percentiles or sample, and 8.0's and later's carry both
in Docker, with performance_schema off the read takes no usage and says usage was not available
in Docker, every step is reported in order with its statements, and a step not asked for is reported skipped
in Docker, an account without the routines' grant of its version fails the rights step naming it, and one without SELECT on performance_schema is a warning naming it

task.done: The scoped live read on the branch; every gate green and in the PR; nothing outside owns touched. After this task a schema is read from a live MySQL of any supported version, 5.7 among them, only as the person chose, the version first, gently and never inside the database, with its metadata and usage as the server gives them and every step reported, ready for the store to keep and the canvas to show.
